newsitem.title: UK: ASDA wary of loyalty card benefits.
newsitem.headline: ASDA wary of loyalty card benefits.

text.p: British supermarket chain ASDA Plc continues to consider launching a loyalty card but chief executive Allan Leighton said it would not do so until it could find a way of getting the most out of a related database.
"I only feel the need for the database (but) people have still not really worked out how to mine the database," he told Reuters in an interview.
He said at the moment, loyalty card schemes appear to provide "useful information," but he wanted one which gave "usable information."
"What we have is a coal mine of useful information and no gold mine of usable information. Show me the goldmine... eventually we could do it," he said.
"I want 25 percent of whatever we do in that area (loyalty cards) to be unmatchable," he said.
ASDA is trialling a loyalty card in selected stores but remains the only one of the big four supermarket chains without a nationwide scheme.
But its market share remains on the increase, easing pressure on the company to join the loyalty card club.
"I don't fundamentally believe that (loyalty) cards are anything but a tactic," Leighton said.
ASDA prides itself on its ability to offer cheaper prices across a basket of goods and Leighton indicated it would prefer to invest here than on loyalty cards.
"If 0.75 percentage point were the cost, well I could do quite a lot with 0.75 percent in terms of pricing," he said.
